record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Characterize all pairs (K, P) consisting of a chiral polytope K and a regular polytope P for which the chirality group of the mix K♦P equals the chirality group of K itself.

evidence.quote: Problem 6 Can we characterize all pairs (K,P) consisting of a chiral polytope K and a regular polytope P such that X(K♦P) = X(K)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup.

An abstract polytope of rank $n$ is a partially ordered set whose elements (faces) satisfy the standard axioms making it locally a "string" incidence structure: it has a minimum and a maximum face, every maximal chain (flag) has exactly $n+2$ elements, it is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition (for any two faces $F<G$ differing in rank by $2$, there are exactly two faces strictly between them). Two flags are called adjacent if they differ in exactly one face.

The automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ of an abstract polytope $\mathcal{P}$ acts freely on the set of flags. The polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is called regular if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts transitively on flags, and chiral if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ has exactly two flag orbits with the property that any two adjacent flags lie in different orbits.

For a chiral polytope $\mathcal{K}$ of rank $n$, fix a base flag and let $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ be the distinguished generators of $\Gamma(\mathcal{K})$ (where $\sigma_i$ corresponds to the rotation interchanging the base flag with its $i$-th adjacent flag composed with the swap to a fixed adjacent flag). The chirality group $X(\mathcal{K})$ is defined as the smallest normal subgroup $N \trianglelefteq \Gamma(\mathcal{K})$ such that $\Gamma(\mathcal{K})/N$ admits an automorphism sending each $\sigma_i$ to $\sigma_i^{-1}$ (with the appropriate corrections in the other generators), i.e., the smallest normal subgroup whose quotient is the rotation group of a regular polytope. The polytope $\mathcal{K}$ is chiral if and only if $X(\mathcal{K}) \neq 1$.

The mix of two polytopes. Given two polytopes $\mathcal{K}$ and $\mathcal{P}$ of the same rank $n$ with rotation/automorphism groups presented as quotients $\Gamma(\mathcal{K}) = W/N_1$ and $\Gamma(\mathcal{P}) = W/N_2$ of a common universal group $W$ (the rotation group of the universal polytope of the appropriate Schläfli type), the mix $\mathcal{K} \diamondsuit \mathcal{P}$ is the poset associated to the group $W/(N_1 \cap N_2)$. When $\mathcal{K}$ is chiral and $\mathcal{P}$ is regular, the mix $\mathcal{K} \diamondsuit \mathcal{P}$ is itself a chiral (or regular) polytope under suitable intersection conditions, and one may consider its chirality group $X(\mathcal{K} \diamondsuit \mathcal{P})$.

Problem. Determine an explicit characterization of all pairs $(\mathcal{K},\mathcal{P})$, where $\mathcal{K}$ is a chiral abstract polytope and $\mathcal{P}$ is a regular abstract polytope of the same rank (and compatible Schläfli type so that the mix is defined), such that
$$X(\mathcal{K} \diamondsuit \mathcal{P}) \;=\; X(\mathcal{K}).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing pairs $(\mathcal{K},\mathcal{P})$ of a chiral and a regular polytope with $X(\mathcal{K}\diamondsuit\mathcal{P})=X(\mathcal{K})$ is stated as an open problem in the literature on chiral polytopes and mixing. The foundational paper by Cunningham on mixing chiral polytopes gives partial criteria (e.g., conditions involving the intersection property and coprimality of Schläfli entries) for the mix to be chiral and for computing its chirality group, but a full characterization is not available. No subsequent work found in the search resolves the general characterization.

status_evidence.title: Mixing chiral polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: By using the chirality group of a polytope, we are able to give simple criteria for when the mix of two polytopes is chiral.
status_evidence.claim: Partial criteria are known for the chirality of mixes via the chirality group, but a general characterization is not established.

status_evidence.title: Constructions for chiral polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions and properties of chiral polytopes including mixes.
status_evidence.claim: Chirality groups of mixes are studied; full characterization of equality X(K♦P)=X(K) not given.
